en: The *Śrīmat Śaṅkarācārya-aṣṭottarasahasranāmāvali*: Oṃ. He who, out of intense compassion, instantly awakens with his lofty rays of wisdom those people whose intellect and vision have been stolen away by immersion in thick darkness, who are nearly dead, whose senses are all abandoned, and who remain only with their breath—he, this Sun among the supreme teachers, Śaṅkara, is our highest deity.

May the illustrious Śaṅkara protect us—he who is radiant with the crescent moon of non-duality as his crest-jewel, who bears the Gaṅgā of pure consciousness, who holds a staff, a fragment of a skull, and an axe in his lotus-like hands, who shines with ornaments of rudrākṣa beads, who is beautiful in his saffron robes and dark antelope skin, who has conquered the death of worldly existence, and who is skilled in swallowing the deadly poison of the fierce serpent known as duality.
Salutations to Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the teacher of all worlds, the physician for those afflicted by the disease of worldly existence, and the treasury of all sciences.

Victory, victory evermore to the eminent Śaṅkarācārya! Victory, victory to his faultless science of non-duality! Victory, victory to his pure life-story in this world! Victory, victory to the devotion of people toward his lotus feet!

Oṃ, salutations to the one whose abode is the glorious Kailāsa. Oṃ, salutations to the one who is as dear as life to Pārvatī. Oṃ, salutations to the one worshipped by the gods beginning with Brahmā. Oṃ, salutations to the one devoted to the protection of his devotees. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose heart is intent on protecting the earth from the dominion of the Buddhists. Oṃ, salutations to the one praised by the gods. Oṃ, salutations to the one who approves of Skanda, who is skilled in revealing the ritual section (Karmakāṇḍa). Oṃ, salutations to the one whose mind honors the human body. Oṃ, salutations to the one who has incited the host of gods.

Oṃ, salutations to him who obtained the earth beyond three thousand oceans of Tiṣya. Oṃ, salutations to him who took refuge in the womb of Āryāmbā, residing in the sacred field of Kālaṭī. Oṃ, salutations to the full moon filling the ocean of the lineage of Śiva and the other gurus. Oṃ, salutations to the son of Śivaguru. Oṃ, salutations to the illustrious one (Śrīmān). Oṃ, salutations to the incarnation of a portion of the true Śiva. Oṃ, salutations to him who was brilliantly named Śaṅkara, a name bestowed by his father that was truly meaningful.

Oṃ, salutations to him who was born in the bright fortnight of the month of Āṣāḍha during the spring season of the year of Īśvara. Oṃ, salutations to him who was born on the fifth lunar day conjoined with the constellation Ārdrā. Oṃ, salutations to the true grandson of Vidyādhirāja. Oṃ, salutations to the one who bestows joy upon the minds of the wise. (20) Oṃ, salutations to him who mastered the sequence of all scripts and languages within his first year. Oṃ, salutations to him who underwent tonsure at the hands of his father before the completion of three years. Oṃ, salutations to him who experienced the sorrow of separation from his father upon reaching his third year.

Oṃ, salutations to the remover of a mother’s grief. Oṃ, salutations to him who is respectful toward service to his mother. Oṃ, salutations to him for whom the mother is a deity. Oṃ, salutations to him for whom the mother is a guru. Oṃ, salutations to him who is like a father to his mother. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose mother was filled with joy upon seeing his childhood play. Oṃ, salutations to the one who was consecrated by a twice-born priest at the command of his mother, according to his own lineage. ||30|| Oṃ, salutations to him who dwelt in the house of a teacher of knowledge. Oṃ, salutations to him who is devoted to the service of his gurus. Oṃ, salutations to him whose forehead shines with the triple mark (*tripuṇḍra*).

Oṃ, salutation to the one who wears the girdle of muñja grass and the deer-skin. Oṃ, salutation to the one who holds a staff of *pālāśa* wood in his hand. Oṃ, salutation to the one clothed in a yellow loincloth. Oṃ, salutation to the one whose neck is adorned with a sacred thread resembling a lotus fiber. Oṃ, salutation to the one devoted to the service of the twilight fires. Oṃ, salutation to the one intent on the study of the rules of discipline. Oṃ, salutation to the one who subsists on alms. ||40|| Oṃ, salutation to supreme bliss. Oṃ, salutation to the one who eternally causes joy to all.

Oṃ, salutations to the Teacher who was made equal [to the gods] by the Vidyā practiced for two or three months. Oṃ, salutations to him who had mastered the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas. Oṃ, salutations to him who has reached the further shore of all branches of knowledge. Oṃ, salutations to him who was satisfied by a single myrobalan fruit from the alms given by a poor Brahmin woman. Oṃ, salutations to him whose mind was distressed upon hearing the words of an unfortunate Brahmin woman. Oṃ, salutations to him who remembered Bhārgava (Paraśurāma) out of a desire to bring relief to the poverty of the twice-born. Oṃ, salutations to him who became a vessel for the grace of Ramā, being pleased by the hymn of praise consisting of a stream of gold.

Oṃ, salutations to him who gladdens the twice-born with the gracious rain of pure golden [teachings]. ||50|| Oṃ, salutations to the one proficient in the science of logic (*tarka-śāstra*). Oṃ, salutations to the one proficient in the Sāṃkhya scriptures. Oṃ, salutations to the one who knows the principles of Patañjali’s system. Oṃ, salutations to the one who knows the true meaning of the Bhaṭṭa school's arguments. Oṃ, salutations to the one possessed of complete knowledge. Oṃ, salutations to the one endowed with glory (*saśrīka*). Oṃ, salutations to the one who bestowed sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*) upon his teacher. Oṃ, salutations to the one devoted to the service of his mother. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose abode is his own home.

Oṃ, salutation to the one who dispels the suffering of his mother, who was weary from the heat of the river’s current. Oṃ, salutation to the one for whom the arising of happiness for his mother was attained through services such as fanning with a fan. Oṃ, salutation to the one who submerged himself while being praised by those approaching him at the riverside dwelling. Oṃ, salutation to the best of rivers located near the house that glows with the boon granted by Pūrṇa. Oṃ, salutation to the one who is the source of grace for his mother, whose heart is filled with the wonder of bliss. Oṃ, salutation to the celestial wish-fulfilling tree that granted the boon of an excellent son to the sovereign of Kerala.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who was gratified by the three plays composed by the Lord of Kerala; Oṃ, salutations to the one whose great intellect rendered the gold presented by the king as insignificant; Oṃ, salutations to the one who honored Dadhīci, Atri, and others who came to his own abode; Oṃ, salutations to the one who delighted the circle of guests through inquiry into the reality of the Self; Oṃ, salutations to the mother who was overwhelmed with grief upon learning the news from the pitcher-born Agastya; Oṃ, salutations to the one who dispelled the mother’s anxiety through persuasion and the awakening of her son to the truth; Oṃ, salutations to the one who loathes the trivial cycle of worldly existence.

Oṃ, salutation to him who yearns for the vision of Truth. Oṃ, salutation to him whose mind is devoted to the fourth stage of life (*turyāśrama*). Oṃ, salutation to the protector of his mother’s command. Oṃ, salutation to him whose lotus-feet were seized by crocodiles at the time of bathing in the Pūrṇā River. Oṃ, salutation to him who was given the command by his mother, who was afflicted with grief due to her affection for her son. Oṃ, salutation to him who released himself from the pain of the crocodile by uttering the *praiṣa* (the sacred syllable). Oṃ, salutation to the one who has conquered the senses. Oṃ, salutation to him whose body was purified by the dust of the lotus-feet of his mother.

Oṃ, homage to him who desires attendance upon his guru. Oṃ, homage to him who requested the instruction of his mother. Oṃ, homage to that most excellent being, vigorous in his commitment to perform the purificatory rites for the body he had promised to bring forth. Oṃ, homage to him who consoled his mother by making her aware of his presence through mere thought. Oṃ, homage to him who was entrusted to his maternal relatives by his own kin. Oṃ, homage to him who removed [her] possessiveness. Oṃ, homage to him who received a blessing as soon as he was born. Oṃ, homage to him who departed from his mother’s house.

Oṃ, salutation to him who was awakened by the words of Anaṅga, which were as terrifying as the waves of a river. Oṃ, salutation to him who removed the suffering of the Gopāla image raised up by his own arm. Oṃ, salutation to him whose form presides over a land liberated from the afflictions of calamities. Oṃ, salutation to him whose mind is intent on beholding the feet of the blessed Govinda. Oṃ, salutation to him who has traversed the great path. Oṃ, salutation to him who dwells upon the banks of the Narmadā. Oṃ, salutation to him who bathes in the Revā, amidst the mass of its surging waves. Oṃ, salutation to him who wears a garment.

Oṃ, salutation to him whose entire body is smeared with ashes. Oṃ, salutation to him who has performed his daily evening rites. Oṃ, salutation to him who is intent on searching for the cave of Govindārya. Oṃ, salutation to him who possesses devotion toward his guru. Oṃ, salutation to him whose eyes are filled with tears of joy born from seeing the cave. Oṃ, salutation to him who has circumambulated the cave. Oṃ, salutation to him who has placed his own body at the entrance. Oṃ, salutation to him who has joined his palms in reverence upon his head. Oṃ, salutation to him who has gratified his teacher by means of hymns of praise.

Oṃ, salutations to him who has communicated the nature of his own self! Oṃ, salutations to him who sought the vision of Brahman! Oṃ, salutations to him whose head was kissed by the feet of the Guru, who was pleased by his hymn of praise! Oṃ, salutations to him who obtained the four great sayings from the mouth of the Noble One’s feet! ||110|| Oṃ, salutations to him who realized the goal of the self through the instruction of the Teacher! Oṃ, salutations to him who bestowed pleasure upon the Teacher! Oṃ, salutations to him who was born from the lotus-like hands of the venerable feet of Govinda! Oṃ, salutations to the one free from anxiety! Oṃ, salutations to the one of regulated diet!

Oṃ, homage to the one who contemplates the reality of the self (ātmatattva). Oṃ, homage to the one afflicted by the fear of harming living beings while on the path during the rainy season. Oṃ, homage to the one who has made his dwelling at the feet of the teacher. Oṃ, homage to the one who observes the commands of the teacher. Oṃ, homage to the one who removes the fear of people submerged in the waters of the five-day rainy season. ||120|| Oṃ, homage to the one whose water-pot is filled with the nectar born of the moon, which is grasped through the perfection of yoga. Oṃ, homage to the one who is fully satisfied by his own conduct, which follows the noble Vedic scriptures.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who praises the Self as awakened by the recognition [arising from] the well-spoken words of Vyāsa. Oṃ, salutations to the one who is subject to the instructions of his spiritual guide. Oṃ, salutations to the one who takes delight in the exposition of the Sūtras. Oṃ, salutations to the one who was eager to go out of a desire to behold Viśveśvara, having received permission from his Guru. Oṃ, salutations to the one who reached the city of the Lord whose crest is the Moon (Śiva). Oṃ, salutations to the one endowed with devotion. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose hand holds a shining staff. Oṃ, salutations to the shaven-headed one. 130. Oṃ, salutations to the one who carries a water-pot. Oṃ, salutations to the one who maintains his vows.

Oṃ, salutation to Him whose body is covered by a loincloth, a patched garment, and a sense of modesty; Oṃ, salutation to Him who has accepted the water-purifier (the *ambupavitra*); Oṃ, salutation to Him whose feet always rest upon wooden sandals (*pādukā*); Oṃ, salutation to Him who has performed his ablutions with the waters of the Gaṅgā; Oṃ, salutation to Him whose lotus-heart is ever serene; Oṃ, salutation to Him who was consecrated as the enemy of the City (Śiva); Oṃ, salutation to the Protector of the Universe who was gratified by the *bilva* fruit; Oṃ, salutation to the Lord of the Universe who is pleased by garlands of beautiful lotuses; Oṃ, salutation to Him whose form is bowed in humility.

Oṃ, salutation to him who was eager to depart far away from the Caṇḍāla on the road to the Gaṅgā. Oṃ, salutation to him who respected the words of the Caṇḍāla, which dispelled the delusion of identifying the body with the Self. Oṃ, salutation to him who was delighted by the questions and follow-up inquiries of Viśveśa, who appeared in the form of a Caṇḍāla. Oṃ, salutation to him who was skilled in composing the hymn consisting of the five verses of wisdom (*manīṣā*). Oṃ, salutation to the Great One. Oṃ, salutation to him who showed the one adorned with the moon on his crest (Śiva) united with his own true nature. Oṃ, salutation to the Self who attained bliss through the joy of that vision. Oṃ, salutation to the one free from all affliction.

Oṃ, homage to the formless one. ||150|| Oṃ, homage to the one free from affliction. Oṃ, homage to the one free from possessiveness. Oṃ, homage to the one devoid of qualities. Oṃ, homage to the all-pervading lord. Oṃ, homage to the eternally satisfied one. Oṃ, homage to the self-blissful one. Oṃ, homage to the unobscured one. Oṃ, homage to the Lord. Oṃ, homage to the eternally pure one. Oṃ, homage to the eternally awakened one. ||160|| Oṃ, homage to the one whose nature is the mass of eternal awakening. Oṃ, homage to the one filled with the grace of the Lord.

Oṃ, salutations to him who is eager for the worship of Īśvara. Oṃ, salutations to him who was impelled to compose the excellent commentary on the Vedānta-sūtras. Oṃ, salutations to the Sovereign. Oṃ, salutations to him whose mind was firmly resolved upon following the command of Īśvara. Oṃ, salutations to him who witnessed the disappearance of Īśvara. Oṃ, salutations to him whose eyes were wide with wonder. Oṃ, salutations to him whose form was most purified by bathing in the river Jāhnavī. Oṃ, salutations to him who meditated incessantly during his daily rites upon the lotus-feet of his Guru. ||170||

Oṃ, salutations to the one who investigates the state of equilibrium (*sāmarasya*) through scripture, reasoning, and personal experience. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose mind is solely inclined toward the welfare of the world. Oṃ, salutations to the one who attained the skill of composing the *Bhāṣya* through the grace of the Lord of the Universe. Oṃ, salutations to the one who has abandoned residence in the city of Kāśī. Oṃ, salutations to the one who contemplates the hermitage of Badarī. Oṃ, salutations to the one who finds great joy in conversing with the multitude of sages dwelling there. Oṃ, salutations to the one who has performed ablutions at various sacred fords (*tīrtha*). Oṃ, salutations to the one who travels on foot.

Oṃ, salutations to Manohara. Oṃ, salutations to him who is endowed with an abundance of bliss from the vision of Badarikāśrama. Oṃ, salutations to him whose supreme non-dual reality has become the fruit of the Karabilvī tree. Oṃ, salutations to him who is expert in warding off the delusion of the world caused by the madman [the Lord]. Oṃ, salutations to him who takes delight in composing profound and gracious great commentaries (Māhābhāṣya). Oṃ, salutations to the Illustrious One (Śrīmān). Oṃ, salutations to him who is eager for the weaving and spreading of the commentaries on the Upaniṣads.

Oṃ, salutations to him who has gratified the three worlds with the essential nectar of the *Gītā-bhāṣya*. Oṃ, salutations to the author of the introductory treatises such as the *Śrīmatsanatsujātīya*. Oṃ, salutations to the one who took great care in composing commentaries on the *Nṛsiṃhatāpanīya* and other Upaniṣads. Oṃ, salutations to the creator of countless works. Oṃ, salutations to the one who acts for the benefit of the world. (190) Oṃ, salutations to the one of sublime intellect. Oṃ, salutations to the one who has shattered all false doctrines through the great reasoning of his *Sūtra-bhāṣya*.

Oṃ, salutations to the sun that dispels the mass of darkness within other commentaries. Oṃ, salutations to him who is intent on teaching all the works he himself composed, beginning with the commentaries. Oṃ, salutations to him who is adorned by a circle of disciples endowed with tranquility, self-restraint, and other virtues. Oṃ, salutations to him whose own commentary is constantly studied by excellent disciples such as Sanandana and others. Oṃ, salutations to him who was resorted to by the illustrious Sanandana after he had thrice studied his commentary on the Self. Oṃ, salutations to him who summoned Sanandana while he was staying on the opposite bank of the Ganges.

Oṃ, salutations to Sanandana, who arrived by way of the multitude of lotuses risen from the Gaṅgā. Oṃ, salutations to him who is devoted to demonstrating the greatness of devotion to the Teacher. Oṃ, salutations to him who was bowed to by Sanandana, whose heart was languid with bliss. Oṃ, salutations to him who is delighted by his embrace. Oṃ, salutations to the indicator of the path of the virtuous. Oṃ, salutations to him who received the renowned title "Padmapāda. Oṃ, salutations to him who is intent upon teaching the Bhāṣya. Oṃ, salutations to the refuter who challenges the scholars assembled at various locations.

Oṃ, salutations to him whose mind is intent on destroying the dense darkness of various false doctrines! Oṃ, salutations to the wise one! Oṃ, salutations to him who is eager to establish the doctrine of non-duality! Oṃ, salutations to the lion roaming in the midst of the great forest of Vedānta! Oṃ, salutations to the bee upon the lotus of the Upaniṣads! Oṃ, salutations to the sun for the lotuses of the Upaniṣads! Oṃ, salutations to him who is intent on experiencing the entire essence of the sweetness of the nectar of non-duality! Oṃ, salutations to the protector of the path of non-duality!

Oṃ, salutation to the contemplator of non-dual Brahman. Oṃ, salutation to the axe that utterly cuts down the forest of duality. Oṃ, salutation to the one who has no rival. Oṃ, salutation to the one whose sole aim is to favor those traveling on the paths of Śruti and Smṛti. Oṃ, salutation to the one of great speech who establishes the multitude of eloquent scholars. Oṃ, salutation to the one who has astonished the throngs of wise men by the play of his own articulate speech. Oṃ, salutation to the one whose ears hear thousands of praises. Oṃ, salutation to the changeless one. Oṃ, salutation to the mine of virtues.

Oṃ, salutations to the one solely devoted to the compendium of the entire essence of the Upaniṣads. Oṃ, salutations to the one capable of extracting the jewel known as the Supreme Self hidden within the Upaniṣads. Oṃ, salutations to the one who has illuminated the surface of the earth with the moonlight of the commentaries on the Upaniṣads. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose essence of eloquent speech resembles the flow of the Gaṅgā. Oṃ, salutations to the Great Sleeper (Mahāśaya). Oṃ, salutations to the wonderful scholar who shattered the elephant-like Vitāṇḍikas. Oṃ, salutations to the one intent upon the propagation of the Bhāṣya. ||230||

Oṃ, salutations to the one eager for the exposition of the commentary. Oṃ, salutations to the one who possesses the essence of knowledge obtained from churning the ocean of the nectar of the commentary. Oṃ, salutations to the one who bestows liberation upon devotees intent on grasping the essence of the commentary. Oṃ, salutations to the one who has purified the three worlds with the mass of glory resulting from composing the commentary. Oṃ, salutations to the one served by ascetics greedy for the taste of the nectar of the commentary. Oṃ, salutations to the one who has brilliantly illuminated the three worlds with the network of light-rays from the jewels of the commentary.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who removes all impurities for those bathed in the waters of the Gaṅgā that is the Bhāṣya. Oṃ, salutations to the one who causes wonder in those who behold the profundity of the Bhāṣya. Oṃ, salutations to the one who bestows liberation upon devotees submerged in the ocean of the Bhāṣya. Oṃ, salutations to the one who is skilled in destroying the darkness [of ignorance] through the radiant rising of the moon that is the Bhāṣya. Oṃ, salutations to the beautiful moon that causes the multitude of night-lotuses known as the Bhāṣya to blossom. Oṃ, salutations to the one who has felled the wicked trees of duality with the multitude of axes that are the arguments of the Bhāṣya.

Oṃ, salutations to him whose intellect is untiring in sporting amidst the waves of the nectar-ocean of the *Bhāṣya*. Oṃ, salutations to him whose mind has become a casket containing the entire essence of the *Bhāṣya*’s established tenets. Oṃ, salutations to him for whom the gold of non-duality (*advaita*) has been purified on the touchstone called the *Bhāṣya*. Oṃ, salutations to him who surpasses the ocean in the vastness and profundity of the *Bhāṣya*. Oṃ, salutations to him who has drenched the surface of the earth with the rain of nectar known as the *Bhāṣya*. Oṃ, salutations to him who has uprooted the succession of sufferings by raining down the ambrosia of the *Bhāṣya*.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who has strung together the flowers of sound reasoning upon the thread of the Bhāṣya. ||250|| Oṃ, salutations to the one whose glory is to be known through the Vedānta. Oṃ, salutations to the one firmly established in the Vedānta. Oṃ, salutations to the one who seeks the goal of the multitude of Vedānta statements. Oṃ, salutations to the one who reveals the intended meaning (*vaidamparya*) shining forth within the Vedānta statements. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose mind is the first to perceive the nectar of the Vedānta statements. Oṃ, salutations to the one who is like a bee tasting the essence of the flowers of the Vedānta statements.

Oṃ, salutations to the one whose mind has become the treasury for the entire essence of the Vedānta. Oṃ, salutations to the swan in the lotus grove of the Vedānta. Oṃ, salutations to the sun for the lotuses of the Vedānta. Oṃ, salutations to the moon-treasury that causes the lilies of the Vedānta to bloom. (260) Oṃ, salutations to the one of noble intellect. Oṃ, salutations to the one who has conquered evil disputants through the assistance of the Vedānta scriptures. Oṃ, salutations to the one who finds ultimate peace in sporting upon the waves of the ocean of the Vedānta. Oṃ, salutations to the one who cuts through the doubts of disciples.

Oṃ, salutations to the one intent on instructing disciples. Oṃ, salutations to the one who appeared as the teacher Vyāsa, disguised in the garb of an elder. Oṃ, salutations to the one impelled by Vyāsa when he desired to know the subject matter being taught. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose own greatness was described by a multitude of disciples. Oṃ, salutations to the source of majesty. Oṃ, salutations to the one delighted by Vyāsa, who was satisfied by hearing his own *sūtra* and *bhāṣya*. (270) Oṃ, salutations to the one who explained the meaning of the *sūtras* when asked. Oṃ, salutations to the eloquent one. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose mind is radiant with discipline.

Oṃ, salutations to him whose mind was gladdened by the inquiry regarding the sūtra beginning with "In that interval" (tadantara); Oṃ, salutations to him who delighted the Brahmins by his words supported by the Vedas; Oṃ, salutations to him who established the movement of the individual soul (jīvātman) when it is affected by subtle elements; Oṃ, salutations to him who demonstrated the statements containing the answers to the questions found in the Tāṇḍi Śruti; Oṃ, salutations to him who formulated his own position in a hundred ways; Oṃ, salutations to the one who effects the complete resolution of all [doubts]; Oṃ, salutations to him who bestowed the greatest wonder upon the great disputing Brahmins. ||280||

Oṃ, salutations to the great sage who was satisfied by the resolution of various questions. Oṃ, salutations to him who has effected the state of aesthetic unity (*sāmarasya*) among the multitude of statements at the conclusion of the Vedas. Oṃ, salutations to the immutable one. Oṃ, salutations to him who engaged in countless debates over eight days. Oṃ, salutations to the recipient of victory. Oṃ, salutations to him whose majesty was praised by listeners filled with wonder and bliss. Oṃ, salutations to him who was awakened by the lotus-feet of Viṣṇu and Śaṅkara, which express the state of being Viṣṇu and Śaṅkara. Oṃ, salutations to him who brought to rest the activity of his own speech as requested by the lotus-feet of Padmā (Lakṣmī).

Oṃ, salutations to the one who knows the essence of his words. Oṃ, salutations to the one intent on offering prostrations. Oṃ, salutations to the knower of the greatness of Vyāsa. Oṃ, salutations to the one devoted to the praise of Vyāsa. Oṃ, salutations to the recipient of the grace of Vyāsa, who is pleased by rows of various verses. Oṃ, salutations to the one eager for the vision of Vyāsa as endowed with his own true form. Oṃ, salutations to the one who reveals the form of Vyāsa, which is as beautiful as a cluster of *tāpiccha* blossoms. Oṃ, salutations to the one surrounded by a multitude of disciples. Oṃ, salutations to the one who performs the act of going out to meet [him].

Oṃ, salutations to him who is intent on earnestly entreating for the pacification of his own transgressions. Oṃ, salutations to him who is striving to touch the pair of lotus-feet of Bādarāyaṇa. Oṃ, salutations to him who proclaims his own fulfillment born from the vision of Vyāsa. Oṃ, salutations to him who makes known the difficulty of composing the multitude of the eighteen Purāṇas. Oṃ, salutations to him who rejoices in being the creator of such a multitude of Purāṇas. Oṃ, salutations to him who praises selflessness in service to others. Oṃ, salutations to the worshiper of Vyāsa.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who praises the division of the four Vedas into separate branches. Oṃ, salutations to the Great One. Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrates his grace toward those whose minds are dull in this age of Kali. Oṃ, salutations to the one who makes known the wonder produced by being the author of various compositions. Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrates the difficulty of the great work known as the *Bhārata*. (310) Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrates that he is an incarnation of Nārāyaṇa. Oṃ, salutations to the one who is intent upon prayer.

Oṃ, salutations to him who announces the arrival of Vyāsa for the sole purpose of bestowing grace. Oṃ, salutations to him who entreated Vyāsa for the sake of illuminating the meaning of his own commentary. Oṃ, salutations to the Sage. Oṃ, salutations to him who was amazed by the profound depth of the Great Sage’s own commentary. Oṃ, salutations to him who was praised by the teacher Vyāsa, the seer of every part of the commentary. Oṃ, salutations to him who was honored by Vyāsa, the seer of the entire essence of his own established doctrine. Oṃ, salutations to him who was worshipped by Vyāsa, the seer of the perfect harmony between the Śruti and the Sūtras.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who is the sole worthy recipient of thousands of words of praise. ||320|| Oṃ, salutations to the Great Sage. Oṃ, salutations to the one honored by Vyāsa, who praised his status as the disciple of Govinda-yogin. Oṃ, salutations to the one who rejoiced in the words of Vyāsa, the proponent of the hundred-fold Śaṅkara. Oṃ, salutations to the one intent upon composing the Bhāṣya that reveals the intention of Vyāsa. Oṃ, salutations to the abode of all auspiciousness. Oṃ, salutations to the bestower of all happiness. Oṃ, salutations to the Omniscient One. Oṃ, salutations to the All-Seeing One.

Oṃ, salutation to the Witness. Oṃ, salutation to the one whose skill is directed in every direction. Oṃ, salutation to the creator of all. Oṃ, salutation to the protector of all. Oṃ, salutation to the one endowed with all majesty. Oṃ, salutation to the knower of the distinctions of all states of being. Oṃ, salutation to the one proficient in all scriptures. Oṃ, salutation to the bestower of all desired objects. Oṃ, salutation to the Divine. Oṃ, salutation to the dispeller of all suffering. Oṃ, salutation to the cutter of all doubts.

Oṃ, homage to the bestower of all prosperity. ||340|| Oṃ, homage to the ordainer of all happiness. Oṃ, homage to him before whom all the immortals bow. Oṃ, homage to him who is worshipped by the entire host of ṛṣis. Oṃ, homage to the cause of all auspiciousness. Oṃ, homage to the remover of all suffering. Oṃ, homage to the gentle one. Oṃ, homage to the inner controller of all. Oṃ, homage to the powerful one. Oṃ, homage to the support of all. Oṃ, homage to the one who goes everywhere. ||350||

Oṃ, salutation to the bestower of auspiciousness in every respect. Oṃ, salutation to the one who possesses the skill of humbling the pride of all wicked disputants. Oṃ, salutation to the mass of fame renowned throughout all the worlds. Oṃ, salutation to the one of unfailing speech. Oṃ, salutation to the deliverer of all devotees. Oṃ, salutation to the warder-off of all calamities. Oṃ, salutation to the one who contemplates the bliss beginning from that of a sovereign emperor up to that of Hiranyagarbha. Oṃ, salutation to the one who was impelled by the venerable Vyāsa to compose numerous and formidable treatises.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who delights in the words of Vyāsa, which seek to dispel the hopes of those who maintain the doctrine of duality. Oṃ, salutations to the one impelled by Vyāsa to understand that he has gone according to his own [true] nature. Oṃ, salutations to the one who awakens others to the composition and dissemination of the Vedānta commentaries. Oṃ, salutations to the one who makes known his own state of having accomplished all that was to be done (*kṛtakṛtyatva*). Oṃ, salutations to the one intent on prayer. Oṃ, salutations to the one who entreats for the presence of Vyāsa at the great sacred site (*mahākṣetra*) of Maṇikarṇī. Oṃ, salutations to the one engaged in the act of relinquishing his own body. Oṃ, salutations to the one who impels Vyāsa.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who observes the command of Vyāsa regarding the abandonment of the prohibited body. Oṃ, salutations to the one impelled by the victory over many unconquered disputants. Oṃ, salutations to the blissful one. Oṃ, salutations to the one who contemplates the completion of the great task of the incarnation. Oṃ, salutations to the one for whom Vyāsa showed respect, being pleased by the sweetness of his own *Sūtra-bhāṣya*. Oṃ, salutations to the one impelled by Vyāsa, who was inspired by the granting of boons. Oṃ, salutations to the poet. Oṃ, salutations to the one who has become a poet eight times as ordained.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who embodies renunciation. Oṃ, salutations to the one who has taken refuge in the eight stages of life brought to perfection through his own genius. Oṃ, salutations to the one who attained the age of sixteen years by the power of Vyāsa’s command. Oṃ, salutations to the one who brings about auspiciousness. Oṃ, salutations to the source of the triple stream consisting of the Śruti, the Sūtras, and the Mahābhāṣya. Oṃ, salutations to Śiva. (380) Oṃ, salutations to the one who finds bliss in touching the pair of lotus feet of Vedavyāsa. Oṃ, salutations to the one who offers a handful of flowers in the form of a flood of words pregnant with devotion.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who accepted the boon granted by Vyāsa. Oṃ, salutations to the one who manifested the disappearance of Vyāsa. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose mind was distressed by the grief of separation from Bādarāyaṇa. Oṃ, salutations to the one who made a singular effort for the conquest of all directions as urged by Vyāsa. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose eyes were fixed upon Kumārila. Oṃ, salutations to the one intent on proceeding toward the southern region. Oṃ, salutations to the one eager for victory over Kumārila, who bears the secondary name Bhaṭṭapāda. Oṃ, salutations to the one prepared to go to Prayāga. ||390||

Oṃ, salutations to him whose form is most purified by bathing at the confluence of the three rivers. Oṃ, salutations to him whose mind is delighted by the sight of the surging mass of waves of the Gaṅgā. Oṃ, salutations to him who is praised by a multitude of charming and faultless verses, like the best of rivers in the sky. Oṃ, salutations to him who has performed his ablutions again and again. Oṃ, salutations to him whose hands are adorned with staffs. Oṃ, salutations to him who recites various mantras for the expiation of sins. Oṃ, salutations to him who is intent upon meditation. Oṃ, salutations to him who is pleased by the chanting of various mantras.

Oṃ, homage to the one who knows the essence of mantras. Oṃ, homage to the supreme one. ||400|| Oṃ, homage to the one capable of explaining the meaning of mantras. Oṃ, homage to the one whose mental domain has become like a casket for the rubies of mantras. Oṃ, homage to the mine of jewel-like mantras. Oṃ, homage to the proud one. Oṃ, homage to the one who reveals the majesty of mantras. Oṃ, homage to the one who knows the reality of the meaning of the mantra-śāstras. Oṃ, homage to the one who propounds the mantra-śāstras. Oṃ, homage to the foremost among practitioners of mantras. ||410||

Oṃ, homage to the venerable one! Oṃ, homage to the bee upon the lotus of mantras! Oṃ, homage to the lion roaming the forest of mantras! Oṃ, homage to the one intent on mantra! Oṃ, homage to the royal swan in the beautiful lake named mantra! Oṃ, homage to the one of great intelligence! Oṃ, homage to the cutter of doubts regarding mantra! Oṃ, homage to the instructor of the various classes of mantras! Oṃ, homage to the one who remembers the Mothers when the time for bathing has arrived! Oṃ, homage to the one of unfailing intellect! ||420||

Oṃ, salutations to him who is intent on the performance of daily rites (*āhnika*). Oṃ, salutations to him who is devoted to the duties of an ascetic (*yatidharma*). Oṃ, salutations to him whose mind is focused on solitude (*ekānta*). Oṃ, salutations to him whose conduct is solitary. Oṃ, salutations to him who has taken refuge in solitude. Oṃ, salutations to him whose sleep was dispelled by the entry of the embers of Bhaṭṭapāda’s foot. Oṃ, salutations to him who was impelled by the desire to compose a commentary (*bhāṣya*) and a sub-commentary (*vārttika*). Oṃ, salutations to him who was eager to witness the life-story of Bhaṭṭapāda. Oṃ, salutations to him who yearned for the light of Kumārila.

Oṃ, homage to him who was eager to depart. ||430|| Oṃ, homage to him who beheld the venerable Bhaṭṭa standing in the midst of a mass of glowing embers. Oṃ, homage to him who revealed that form surrounded by excellent disciples such as Prabhākara and others. Oṃ, homage to him who was filled with wonder at the gracious sight of his face while situated in the glowing embers. Oṃ, homage to him who was greeted by the venerable Bhaṭṭa, who was pleased by his unexpected arrival. Oṃ, homage to him for whom various services were performed by the excellent disciples of the venerable Bhaṭṭa. Oṃ, homage to him who satisfied Kumārila by manifesting his presence at the time of his final passing.

Oṃ, salutation to him who was praised by the venerable Bhaṭṭa, who was satisfied by his own vision. Oṃ, salutation to him who was honored by Bhaṭṭa, who spoke of the greatness of associating with the virtuous. Oṃ, salutation to him who was mourned for by Bhaṭṭa, who spoke of the impermanence of saṃsāra. Oṃ, salutation to him who extolled the words of the venerable Bhaṭṭa, which provide awakening to the uncertainty of time. Oṃ, salutation to him who listened well to the discourse on the fault of the extreme [view] that denies the Lord (Īśvara). Oṃ, salutation to him who praised the speech of Bhaṭṭa, whose awakening resulted from being a disciple of a Buddhist.

Oṃ, salutations to him who was distressed upon hearing of the fall from the roof of the palace belonging to the venerable Bhaṭṭapāda. Oṃ, salutations to him who dispelled the fear of this injury by means of his application of devotion to the Vedas. Oṃ, salutations to him who consoled the weeping Bhaṭṭa who was grieving over the loss of one of his eyes. Oṃ, salutations to him who was distressed upon hearing of the occurrence of the misfortune known as the offense against his guru. Oṃ, salutations to him who showed the entry into a fire of chaff (tuṣāgni) prepared for the purpose of performing an expiation. Oṃ, salutations to him who was honored by the words of Bhaṭṭa, which awakened the realization of the fulfillment arising from his own vision.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who proclaimed the absence of fortune for the composition of a commentary on his own work; oṃ, salutations to the one who caused Bhaṭṭa to lament the absence of fame resulting from that [commentary]; oṃ, salutations to the one who praised the speech of Bodhibhaṭṭa regarding the notification of his own incarnation; oṃ, salutations to the one who made known his descent as Subrahmaṇya; oṃ, salutations to the one devoted to praise; oṃ, salutations to the one who made known his own scriptures for the purpose of establishing the *karmakāṇḍa*; oṃ, salutations to the one who made known his own vows for the purpose of instructing others in the path of the virtuous.

Oṃ, salutation to him whose mind is eager for life by the sprinkling of drops of water from his hand. Oṃ, salutation to him who acts in accordance with the venerable Bhaṭṭa regarding the unbearable nature of public censure. Oṃ, salutation to him who approves of the venerable Bhaṭṭa’s exclusive devotion to the vows prescribed in the scriptures. Oṃ, salutation to him who acts to avoid ill-repute arising from the transgression of what is taught in the scriptures. Oṃ, salutation to him who serves the venerable Bhaṭṭa while desiring his own fulfillment of all duties. Oṃ, salutation to him who fulfills the longing of the venerable Bhaṭṭa, who seeks the Brahma-vidyā known as Tāraka.

Oṃ, salutation to the one impelled by the great scholar named Maṇḍana for the sake of victory. Oṃ, salutation to the friend. Oṃ, salutation to the one urged on by the venerable Bhaṭṭapāda, who praised his quality of erudition. Oṃ, salutation to the one who listened to the account of him who was devoted to the path of worldly activity (*pravṛttimārga*). Oṃ, salutation to the one who clearly indicated the duty to strive for the victory of the noble Maṇḍana. Oṃ, salutation to the one who listened to the state of his speech arising from the curse of Durvāsas. Oṃ, salutation to the one recognized as the foremost disciple of Bhaṭṭa. Oṃ, salutation to the ocean of realized knowledge (*vijñāna*).

Oṃ, salutation to him who was impelled by the performance of numerous debates witnessed by Bhāratī. Oṃ, salutation to him who made the hearing of victory for others dependent solely upon his own victory. Oṃ, salutation to him who was honored by the report of his fitness for composing the Vārtika treatise. Oṃ, salutation to him who was approved by Bhaṭṭa, who requested his presence for a mere moment. Oṃ, salutation to him who fulfilled Kumārila’s purpose by explaining the Tāraka-Brahman. Oṃ, salutation to him who was meditated upon by the venerable Bhaṭṭa, the knower of the reality of supreme non-duality. Oṃ, salutation to him who was intent upon bestowing grace upon Bhaṭṭa.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who has entered the abode of Viṣṇu. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose residence is adorned by having reached the path of the sky. Oṃ, salutations to the one who beheld the loveliness of the city named Māhiṣmatī. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose entire hermitage was shaken by winds mingled with the spray of the Revā river. ||480|| Oṃ, salutations to the one who performed his ablutions in the Revā river. Oṃ, salutations to the one devoted to his daily rituals. Oṃ, salutations to the one who beheld the maidservant of that [city] on the path of his vision. Oṃ, salutations to the one endowed with greatness.

Oṃ, salutation to the one who asks the way to the great palace worthy of adornment. Oṃ, salutation to the one of great renown. Oṃ, salutation to the one to whom an answer was given by a maidservant overwhelmed with wonder. Oṃ, salutation to the one of noble speech. Oṃ, salutation to the one whose house was indicated by a parrot that propounded self-validity (*svataḥprāmāṇya*) and other doctrines. Oṃ, salutation to the one whose house was indicated by a parrot that conversed with the Lord of Karma (*Karmeśvara*) and others. Oṃ, salutation to the one whose body [and] dwelling were indicated by a parrot propounding the state of being the sustainer of the world (*jagaddhṛvatva*) and other qualities. Oṃ, salutation to the one intent on praising the words of a parrot confined within a nest at the door.

Oṃ, homage to the one who has entered the place of adornment, recognized by the aforementioned signs! Oṃ, homage to the one who considers the protection of the door, the difficulty of entry, and the movement within the interior of the house! Oṃ, homage to the one who traverses the path of the sky fashioned through the majesty of yoga! Oṃ, homage to the one who springs up within the courtyard! Oṃ, homage to the one who has surveyed the house on all sides! Oṃ, homage to the one who beholds the beauty of the great mansion that reaches the clouds! Oṃ, homage to the one who gazes upon the noble lady adorned with ornaments born from the rays of the Lotus-Born One!

Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrated the washing of the feet of Vyāsa and Jaimini when they were invited. ||500|| Oṃ, salutations to the one who was utterly amazed by the sight of Vyāsa and Jaimini appearing together. Oṃ, salutations to the one honored by Vyāsa and Jaimini, who manifested their presence at that very moment. Oṃ, salutations to the one beheld by Maṇḍana, who had suddenly arrived as an ascetic. Oṃ, salutations to the one who humbled the noble Maṇḍana, who was devoted to the path of worldly activity (*pravṛtti-mārga*). Oṃ, salutations to the one skilled in resolving those [objections] with reproachful words.

Oṃ, salutations to the one whose intellect is expert in providing answers to all questions that ought to be adorned. Oṃ, salutations to Maṇḍana, who was rendered speechless by the cleverness of the web of *vakrokti* (paradoxical speech). Oṃ, salutations to the one who dispelled the night of the faults perceived in the ascetic’s censure through the words of Vyāsa. Oṃ, salutations to the one shown by Vyāsa to be the very embodiment of Viṣṇu himself. Oṃ, salutations to Maṇḍana Ārya, who was invited under the authority of Vyāsa’s command. Oṃ, salutations to the recipient of the many rites of worship performed by Maṇḍana Ārya.

Oṃ, salutations to him who fashioned his summons for the sake of alms; Oṃ, salutations to him who begs solely for the alms of debate; Oṃ, salutations to him who seeks only the alms of disputation and awakens others to their own scriptures; Oṃ, salutations to him who demonstrates the making of a wager to attain the status of mutual disciples; Oṃ, salutations to him whose begging for food is disregarded; Oṃ, salutations to him who is devoted to the alms of debate; Oṃ, salutations to him who makes known the desire for the mere expansion of the path of the Upanishads; Oṃ, salutations to him who was praised by the noble Maṇḍana, who was filled with wonder and bliss.

Oṃ, homage to Maṇḍana, who was satisfied by the discourse of the long-desired true debate (sadvāda). Oṃ, homage to the noble Maṇḍana, who praised the one striving for alms in the form of debate. Oṃ, homage to the one impelled by the ornament of awakening (bodhi) through the realization of the emptiness of witnesses in dispute. Oṃ, homage to the noble Maṇḍana, who praised the one seeking the status of witness for the two classes of sages. Oṃ, homage to the one whose mind is eager for debate, having established neutrality through the Goddess of Speech (Bhāratī). Oṃ, homage to the one who demonstrated the desire to know [the truth] through the binding of the formal proposition and other elements of debate.

Oṃ, salutation to the one who performed immeasurable services such as sowing seeds for Maṇḍanārya. Oṃ, salutation to the one devoted to the presence and conversation with Vyāsa and Jaimini. Oṃ, salutation to the one who manifested the internal dissolution of the two sages. Oṃ, salutation to the one who emerged from the abode of the lord of the twice-born. Oṃ, salutation to the one who made his residence in the temple situated near the river Revā. Oṃ, salutation to the one devoted to private conversation with his own circle of disciples. Oṃ, salutation to the one resorted to by rows of disciples to whom he had proclaimed all subjects of knowledge.

Oṃ, salutations to him who contemplates the difficulty of attaining the presence of Vyāsa and Jaimini. Oṃ, salutations to him who longs for the passing of the three watches of the night. Oṃ, salutations to him who is devoted to the morning bath. Oṃ, salutations to him who has performed his daily religious duties. Oṃ, salutations to him who is surrounded by a circle of disciples. Oṃ, salutations to him whose form serves as the ornament to the great mansion of Maṇḍanārya. Oṃ, salutations to him who has reached a definitive conclusion regarding the meaning of disputes. Oṃ, salutations to him who is honored by Maṇḍana.

Oṃ, salutation to the one who manifests the presence of eloquence shining through the members of the assembly (sadasya). Oṃ, salutation to the one who praises the noble [opponent] adorned and prepared for the act of debate. Oṃ, salutation to the one whose mind is delighted by the union of the members of the assembly and the disputant. Oṃ, salutation to the one who exerts himself in making the formal proposition (pratijñā). Oṃ, salutation to the one who indicates the essential purport of the Vedānta. Oṃ, salutation to the one who demonstrates the oneness with Brahman appearing in the form of the entire universe. Oṃ, salutation to the one whose nature is illusory, as demonstrated by examples such as silver in a mother-of-pearl shell.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who makes known the state of abiding in one’s own self, which is attainable solely through the knowledge of Brahman. ||550|| Oṃ, salutations to the one who propounds liberation untouched by rebirth. Oṃ, salutations to the one intent upon revealing the authority of the collection that constitutes the pinnacle of the three Vedas. Oṃ, salutations to the one who makes known the whiteness of the garment to be attained by one who has been victorious. Oṃ, salutations to the one who makes known his status as the witness to the speech of those belonging to the factions of victory and defeat. Oṃ, salutations to the one eager to hear all the propositions of Viśvarūpa.

Oṃ, salutations to him who is distressed by hearing those statements that teach the non-authoritativeness of the Vedānta; oṃ, salutations to him who is agitated by hearing the claims of the authority of the words of the Karmakāṇḍa; oṃ, salutations to him who is capable of listening only to the mere words of the Kriyā-yogins; oṃ, salutations to him who shows the seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍana) as being attainable through ritual action alone. Oṃ, salutations to him who listens to the declarations that one must perform the web of rituals for as long as life lasts; oṃ, salutations to him who approves of the words of those who have been defeated yet still cling to their own saffron robes.

Oṃ, salutations to the one engaged in debate with innumerable opponents, witnessed by Sarasvatī. Oṃ, salutations to the Lord of Ascetics (Yatīśvara). Oṃ, salutations to the one who has commenced a dispute at the conclusion of his daily morning rituals. Oṃ, salutations to the one who wears a beautiful garland hanging from his own neck, offered by Sarasvatī. Oṃ, salutations to the one who displays the beauty of the garland hanging from his neck, which is worthy of being adorned. Oṃ, salutations to the one who makes the night of defeat vanish for Mālatī, who was wearing that garland. Oṃ, salutations to the one to whom the Goddess of Speech (Vāṇī), while occupied with household chores, gave excellent alms-food.

Oṃ, homage to the one whose intellect is untiring despite the disputes initiated by the monk Uttara-kṣaṇa. Oṃ, homage to the one whose nectar-like words were drunk by Brahmā and others as they sat above. Oṃ, homage to the one of great speech, free from defects such as anger, verbal faults, and birth. Oṃ, homage to the one who refutes the arguments of Maṇḍana, who was intent on refuting non-duality. Oṃ, homage to the one eager to shatter the doctrines asserting the difference between the individual soul, the Lord, and the world. Oṃ, homage to the one who demonstrates the dialogues and other discourses such as those between Uddālaka and Śvetaketu.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who establishes the natural meaning of the flood of statements such as "That thou art" (tat tvam asi). Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrates the groundlessness of the claim that [the Upanishads] are subordinate to ritual injunctions (vidhi-śeṣa). Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrates the intended meaning contained within distinct contexts (prakaraṇa). Oṃ, salutations to the one whose supreme aim is the eradication of the doctrine that [the Upanishads] are for the purpose of meditative worship (upāsanā). Oṃ, salutations to the one who reveals the intended meaning of the scriptures as resting solely in non-dualism (kevalādvaita). Oṃ, salutations to the one intent upon the exposition of the Self whose nature is Being-Consciousness-Bliss (sac-cid-ānanda). ||580||

Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrates the logical reasoning that [the opponent's position] is useful only for the purpose of recitation; Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrates the superior strength of the flood of statements concerning non-dual awakening; Oṃ, salutations to the one capable of uprooting every aspect of the validity of the cognition of duality; Oṃ, salutations to the one who establishes the absence of authority in the flood of statements that display duality; Oṃ, salutations to the one intent upon demonstrating the weakness of the perception of duality; Oṃ, salutations to the one who explains the intended meaning of the thousands of utterances censuring duality.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrates that [the scriptures] merely restate distinctions well-known in the world. Oṃ, salutations to the one who establishes the authority of the statements regarding the awakening to non-duality, though it is not commonly known. Oṃ, salutations to the one who displays various illustrative examples. Oṃ, salutations to the one who points to the words of the Śruti. ||590|| Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrates his own direct experience, constructed from thousands of logical arguments. Oṃ, salutations to the one who displays the great friendship between Śruti and logic. Oṃ, salutations to the one free from envy.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who displays the partiality of causal defects and who casts off and refutes [false] ornaments. Oṃ, salutations to the one who awakens [others] to the fact that [duality] is conditioned by limiting adjuncts (*upādhi*). Oṃ, salutations to the one who reveals true non-duality (*advaita*). Oṃ, salutations to the one whose mind is solely intent on the means for realizing the Supreme Brahman, which is beyond saṃsāra. Oṃ, salutations to the one who proclaims the identity of the individual soul (*kṣetrajña*) and the Supreme Self (*paramātman*), and who points to the *Gītā* and other scriptures. Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrates the attainment of the state free from phenomenal proliferation (*niṣprapañcatva*) through the removal of superimpositions (*adhyāropa-apavāda*). Oṃ, salutations to the one who refutes the doctrines of wicked disputants by composing thousands of logical arguments. ||600||

Oṃ, homage to the one who displays the garland hanging from the neck of Maṇḍanīya. Oṃ, homage to the one covered by a rain of flowers. Oṃ, homage to the one gladdened by Bhāratī. Oṃ, homage to the one who showed Bhāratī when she arrived at the time for alms. Oṃ, homage to the one intent on praising the eloquence of Vāṇī, which summoned both [of them]. Oṃ, homage to the one who heard the account of his own curse awakened by Bhāratī. Oṃ, homage to the one who listened to the news of that curse exceeding [the duration of] Jaya’s [life]. Oṃ, homage to the self-controlled one (vaśin).

Oṃ, salutations to the one who obstructed Bhāratī as she was intent on returning to her own abode. Oṃ, salutations to the one who rendered the speech of Vanadurgā’s great mantra effective. Oṃ, salutations to the one who made known his status as an incarnation of Sarasvatī. Oṃ, salutations to the foremost among the knowers of the Vedas. Oṃ, salutations to the one who made known his dependence upon those possessed of devotion. Oṃ, salutations to the one resplendent with humility. Oṃ, salutations to the one intent on praying for residence in the mortal world until the end of his own permission. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose activity proceeded from knowledge that [the world] should be adorned.

Oṃ, salutations to the one free from longing. Oṃ, salutations to the one who dispels the doubts concerning that [Self] which have been overcome by the dullness born of ritual action (*karma*). Oṃ, salutations to the one who listens to the discourse on the absence of suffering arising from one's own defeat. Oṃ, salutations to the one who enlightens Maṇḍana, who was grieving due to his hopelessness regarding the arguments of Jaimini. ||620|| Oṃ, salutations to the one who reveals Jaimini’s intention as being one that favors [liberation] according to desire. Oṃ, salutations to the one who teaches that [ritual action] is merely an indirect means (*praṇāḍī*). Oṃ, salutations to the one approved by Jaimini. Oṃ, salutations to the one who proclaims knowledge as having liberation alone as its direct fruit.

Oṃ, salutation to the one of great speech. Oṃ, salutation to the one who elaborates upon the impossibility of the accumulation of karma being the giver of results. Oṃ, salutation to the one who establishes that the Lord alone is the giver of results. Oṃ, salutation to the one who makes known the logical reasoning. Oṃ, salutation to the one capable of uncovering the intended meaning of the web of words of Jaimini. Oṃ, salutation to the one who indicates that the purport [of Jaimini] is merely the absence of an inferable Lord. Oṃ, salutation to the one who reveals the intention of Jaimini, who maintains that the Lord is knowable through the Veda alone. Oṃ, salutation to the one who gazes upon the noble lady Āryā, the ornament of whose heart was swinging like a swing.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who spoke for Jaimini, who had come to dispel his doubts. Oṃ, salutations to the one who spoke for Jaimini, so that he might understand the correctness of all the aspects taught by [the Lord] himself. Oṃ, salutations to the state of omniscience proclaimed by Jaimini. Oṃ, salutations to the one worshipped by Jaimini. Oṃ, salutations to the one who was greeted by Jaimini, which indicated his own incarnation. Oṃ, salutations to the one who revealed the essential meaning of the words of Jaimini and Vyāsa. Oṃ, salutations to the one who manifested the disappearance of Jaimini.

Oṃ, homage to the one who is the vessel of victory in every respect. ||640|| Oṃ, homage to the one who brings about the grace of the Noble One (Ārya), the ornament of those prostrating with the eight-limbed salutation. Oṃ, homage to the one who is greeted by the Noble One (Āryā), the ornament of those who recognize their own incarnations. Oṃ, homage to the one who is devoted to the Noble One (Ārya), the ornament of those who grieve for their own lack of realization. Oṃ, homage to the one who rejoices in the words of Maṇḍana, who grieves for his own karmic dullness. Oṃ, homage to the one who rejoices in the words of Maṇḍana, which awaken one from the suffering of saṃsāra.

Oṃ, salutations to the one honored by Maṇḍana while sporting amidst waves of supreme bliss. Oṃ, salutations to the one who proclaims the seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) that dispels the darkness of one's own ignorance. Oṃ, salutations to the one capable of rescuing the Supreme Self seized by the demoness of nescience (avidyā). Oṃ, salutations to the one entreated by the noble Maṇḍana, who expects forgiveness for his own transgressions. Oṃ, salutations to the one who justified his own incarnation through the efforts of the noble Maṇḍana. Oṃ, salutations to the one worshipped by Maṇḍana, who praises his own previously acquired merit.

Oṃ, homage to the one who is exceedingly delighted by the adornment of perfect self-realization. Oṃ, homage to the one who praises the seat of awakening (bodhimaṇḍa) which is extremely difficult to attain through self-realization. Oṃ, homage to the one whose mind is perfectly satisfied by the composition of various words of praise. Oṃ, homage to the one who is lauded by the countless salutations and hymns composed by the noble Maṇḍana. Oṃ, homage to the one who is the recipient of the thousands of brief praises fashioned by Maṇḍana. Oṃ, homage to the one who is eager to bestow grace upon Maṇḍana, who has gone for refuge at his own feet.

Oṃ, homage to the one who praises the adornment of the seat of awakening through the realization of being his own servant. Oṃ, homage to the one whose mind is made tremulous by great devotion for that which is to be adorned. Oṃ, homage to the one whose mind is intent upon bringing about the fruitfulness of his [the Lord’s] birth. Oṃ, homage to the one who praises Maṇḍana, who was intent on renouncing son, wife, and home. Oṃ, homage to the one eager to secure the consent of the wife who is to be adorned. Oṃ, homage to the one who is fully rejoiced in by the speech of the Sage, who knows all his conduct.

Oṃ, homage to the one who attained the status of a disciple through Maṇḍana and praised the words of Bodhi; Oṃ, homage to the one who reflected upon the true nature of all matters spoken by the Sage; Oṃ, homage to the one who contemplated the speech of Bodhivāṇī regarding the absence of total victory; Oṃ, homage to the one who considered the eloquence of Vāṇī, which expressed that [the opponent] possessed only half of the share; Oṃ, homage to the one intent on exposing the faults in the conversation with women; Oṃ, homage to the one who honored the speech and utterances of Vāṇī as she witnessed the dispute between Yājñavalkya and his wife.

Oṃ, homage to the one who reflected upon the arguments and counter-arguments regarding easily obtainable vessels and the like. ||670|| Oṃ, homage to the one who dwells in the midst of assemblies of the learned. Oṃ, homage to the one who engages in dialogues with Vāṇī. Oṃ, homage to the one by whom the essence of nectar has been surpassed through the union with the sweetness of a torrent of speech. Oṃ, homage to the one whose majesty is invincible in all the scriptures contemplated by Bhāratī. Oṃ, homage to the one who took up the renunciate life in extreme childhood. Oṃ, homage to the one who turned his back on the flood of sense objects. Oṃ, homage to the one who posed questions concerning the science of love (kāmaśāstra).

Oṃ, homage to him whose supreme mind is fixed on contemplation. Oṃ, homage to him who is apprehensive of public censure. Oṃ, homage to him who promotes the dharma of the ascetic. Oṃ, homage to him who is intent on manifesting externally his ignorance of the science of erotics. Oṃ, homage to him who requested [permission] with a limit of only one month. Oṃ, homage to him who was granted leave by Vāṇī. Oṃ, homage to him who possesses self-mastery. Oṃ, homage to him who made an effort for the purpose of departing. Oṃ, homage to him who is adorned by a row of disciples. Oṃ, homage to him who traveled through the sky by means of the power of yoga.

Oṃ, salutations to the knower of the reality of yoga. Oṃ, salutations to him who beheld the body of King Gatacetana. Oṃ, salutations to him of the delighted intellect. Oṃ, salutations to him who revealed the royal body covered by the womenfolk. Oṃ, salutations to him whose mind was eager for entry into that body. Oṃ, salutations to him who was intent on being questioned by his excellent disciples such as Sanandana. Oṃ, salutations to him whose departure was forbidden by the lotus-feet of the most devoted [Padmā]. Oṃ, salutations to the observer of vows.

Oṃ, salutation to the one whose nature is to attract the objects described by Sanandana; Oṃ, salutation to the one who makes known the lotus-feet that dispel doubts regarding the vow of perpetual celibacy (*ūrdhvaretas*); Oṃ, salutation to the one who warded off [the threat] through his lotus-feet for those fearing laxity in the dharma of renunciation (*saṃnyāsa*); Oṃ, salutation to the one who makes known the arising of sin only in one who possesses the conceit of a body; Oṃ, salutation to the one who makes known the absence of taint from the flood of actions for one who is free from egoism (*nirahaṃkāra*); Oṃ, salutation to the one who makes known that the Self, hidden in the cave of the heart, must be protected within its own body.

Oṃ, salutation to the one who has attained a royal body renowned as that of an immortal; Oṃ, salutation to the knower of distinctions; Oṃ, salutation to the bearer of the royal body moved by his own entry; Oṃ, salutation to the one who astonished the women there by the sudden restoration of life; Oṃ, salutation to the one eager to behold the multitude of joyful women; Oṃ, salutation to the one greeted by the chief ministers filled with wonder and bliss; Oṃ, salutation to the one intent on hearing the resounding blast of conchs and drums. ||710||

Oṃ, homage to the one who produces joy for all people! Oṃ, homage to the bestower of auspiciousness! Oṃ, homage to the one for whom his own rites of pacification have been performed by the domestic priest! Oṃ, homage to the one who is a refuge for tranquility! Oṃ, homage to the one for whom auspicious ceremonies have been performed! Oṃ, homage to the one mounted upon a noble elephant! Oṃ, homage to the one who is free from worldly desire! Oṃ, homage to the one for whom honors have been rendered by ministers and others! Oṃ, homage to the one esteemed by the virtuous! Oṃ, homage to the one intent upon protecting the earth! Oṃ, homage to the one who knows the distinction between dharma and adharma! ||720||

Oṃ, homage to the one thoroughly proficient in the path of policy! Oṃ, homage to the protector of royal affairs! Oṃ, homage to the vessel of the ministers' confidence, produced by his own nobility and other virtues! Oṃ, homage to the one who gladdens the virtuous with the multitude of his own qualities! Oṃ, homage to the one honored by the ministers, who know him to be capable of entering the bodies of others! Oṃ, homage to the one upon whom the entire burden of the kingdom has been placed by the ministers! Oṃ, homage to the lord of the earth! Oṃ, homage to the one who makes his residence in the inner apartments! Oṃ, homage to the one served by women!

Oṃ, homage to the one who has attained the great festival of various sports within the body of the protector of the earth. Oṃ, homage to the one who is turned away from the bliss of sense objects. Oṃ, homage to the one who censures the flood of sense objects. Oṃ, homage to the one who pacifies the enemies that are sense objects. Oṃ, homage to the one whose intellect is extremely remote from sense objects. Oṃ, homage to the one who acts as an axe for cutting down the great forest known as sense objects. Oṃ, homage to the one who is untouched by the contact with the poisonous flames known as sense objects. Oṃ, homage to the one who observes the vow of silence (or self-restraint). Oṃ, homage to the one who acts like the crest of the submarine fire that dries up the ocean of sense objects.

Oṃ, homage to the one whose inner body is far removed from the six enemies, such as desire and anger. Oṃ, homage to the one who reveals the worthlessness of sense objects. Oṃ, homage to the one whose inner being is undisturbed by sense objects. Oṃ, homage to the lion intent on subduing the herd of elephants known as sense objects. Oṃ, homage to the destroyer of the pride of the tigers of sense objects. Oṃ, homage to the physician for the serpents of sense objects. Oṃ, homage to the one who contemplates the insurmountable nature of the flood of sense objects. Oṃ, homage to the one free from fickleness.

Oṃ, salutation to him who is eager to grasp the very essence of the *Vātsānaya-kalā-sāra*. Oṃ, salutation to him who has experienced countless enjoyments within the bodies of kings. Oṃ, salutation to him who assumes the guise of a sovereign. Oṃ, salutation to him who is mindful of the circle of disciples regarding the awakening [necessary] at the time of the transgression of the *samaya*. Oṃ, salutation to him who is mindful of the circle of his own disciples submerged in the ocean of suffering. Oṃ, salutation to him who seeks out the circle of disciples bewildered as to what ought to be done. Oṃ, salutation to him who recognized the splendor of the disciples who were listeners when the king rose from the dead.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who gazes upon his own disciples, who are enriched by various delightful appearances. Oṃ, salutations to the one who listens to the Nāga among his disciples, who possesses extreme proficiency in the science of song. Oṃ, salutations to the one who listens well to the beautiful verses composed as instructions by others. Oṃ, salutations to the one who contemplates the meaning of the words spoken by his disciples, which contain various profound meanings. Oṃ, salutations to the one who takes delight in hearing the statements woven with the meaning of Vedānta. Oṃ, salutations to the one who contemplates the meaning of the statements "That thou art" and so forth, as uttered by his disciples.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who contemplates the Supreme Self, hidden within all the Vedāntas. Oṃ, salutations to the one who knows the disposition of his own disciples. Oṃ, salutations to the one who caused [the disciple] to enter his own body. Oṃ, salutations to the one who showed the self-body being intensely scorched. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose mind was swift. Oṃ, salutations to the one who contemplated the means for pacifying the suffering of that time. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose soul was resolved upon the hymn of praise to Lakṣmī-Nṛsiṃha. Oṃ, salutations to the one who composed beautiful verses. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose body is Śrī-Nṛsiṃha, pleased by the weaving together of various words of praise.

Oṃ, homage to Him whose body is the tranquility of Nṛsiṃha’s compassion for those who have taken refuge. Oṃ, homage to Him whose two sides are surrounded by excellent disciples such as Sanandana and others. Oṃ, homage to Him intent upon recounting His own life story. Oṃ, homage to Him who understands the state of being a disciple. Oṃ, homage to Him who travels through the path of the sky. Oṃ, homage to Him who gazes upon the dwelling of Maṇḍanārya. Oṃ, homage to Him who delights Maṇḍanārya, who is averse to the tasting of sense objects. Oṃ, homage to Him to whom Maṇḍanārya offered countless prostrations and joined palms in reverence.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who praises the noble ones who adorn their minds with the resolve for renunciation. Oṃ, salutations to the one who rests in the posture of sitting upon a seat. Oṃ, salutations to the one who has been beheld by Śāradā. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose own omniscience was extolled by Śāradā. ||780|| Oṃ, salutations to the one who is eager for debate. Oṃ, salutations to the one who manifested the disappearance of Bāṇa as he prepared to go to his own abode. Oṃ, salutations to the one intent on speaking words that revealed the majesty of Yoga. Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrated the state of being the wife of Brahmā.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who reveals its majesty. Oṃ, salutations to the one who desires to dwell in sacred fields such as Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, which he himself has envisioned. Oṃ, salutations to the one intent on praying for the presence [of the deity] in excellent sacred fields such as Śṛṅgagiri. Oṃ, salutations to the one pleased by the presence in the sacred field authorized by Bhāratī. Oṃ, salutations to the one who manifested a sudden disappearance. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose mind was overwhelmed with wonder. Oṃ, salutations to the one who approved of the noble lady’s offering of all her possessions and ornaments according to the prescribed rites.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who instructs in all the rites prescribed by the *Sannyāsa-gṛhya-vidhi*. Oṃ, salutations to the four Great Sayings (*mahāvākya*) spoken by the illustrious Maṇḍana Miśra and Karṇa. Oṃ, salutations to the listener of the entire reality-meaning contained within the Great Sayings. Oṃ, salutations to the Guru. Oṃ, salutations to the one who establishes the denoted meaning and the indicated meaning of the words "That" (*tat*) and "Thou" (*tvam*). Oṃ, salutations to the one who brings about the realization of the unity of both indicated meanings. Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrates various illustrative examples. Oṃ, salutations to the method for uprooting, from their very foundation, the sense of "I" and "mine" regarding the body and other such things.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrated the parable of the Great Fish as proclaimed in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad. Oṃ, salutations to the one who established the absence of connection with the self in states such as waking. Oṃ, salutations to the one devoted to the support of the doctrine of illusory manifestation (*vivartavāda*). Oṃ, salutations to the one whose supreme non-dual reality was determined through the indicative marks of purport (*tātparyaliṅga*). Oṃ, salutations to the one who revealed the greatness of the Guru. Oṃ, salutations to the knower of reality. Oṃ, salutations to the awakener of reality. Oṃ, salutations to the one who caused the Lord of the Gods (*Sureśvara*) to fall at the glance of his own pair of feet.

Oṃ, homage to him whose side-glances, embraced by compassion, have destroyed the inner darkness of impurity. Oṃ, homage to the giver of the name Sureśvara. Oṃ, homage to him who is well-worshipped by Sureśvara. Oṃ, homage to the dweller on the banks of the Narmadā. Oṃ, homage to him who is eager to go to Śrīśaila. Oṃ, homage to the beholder of Mallikārjuna. Oṃ, homage to the one who has performed prostrations before Bhramarāmbā. Oṃ, homage to the one who is attended by a circle of disciples who have conquered the Māheśvaras and others.

Oṃ, homage to the moon of the moonlight of fame spreading through all directions. Oṃ, homage to him who was bowed to by the Kāpālika who was listening to his own majesty. Oṃ, homage to him for whom many networks of hymns were composed by the Kāpālika. Oṃ, homage to the one who is indifferent [to praise]. (820) Oṃ, homage to him who listened well to the statement regarding his own departure for the sake of pleasing the Kapālin. Oṃ, homage to him who reflected upon the difficult words expected from the head of the Omniscient One. Oṃ, homage to him who reflected upon the words of the Kāpāla spoken as an expression of his own omniscience.

Oṃ, salutation to the one to whom the Kāpālika, intent on requesting his own head, has offered obeisance. Oṃ, salutation to the one who is devoted to perceiving the faults of his own body, which is full of many impurities. Oṃ, salutation to the one who is devoted to observing the vow of selflessness toward the welfare of others. Oṃ, salutation to the one whose inner being is unperturbed by the departure of his own body. Oṃ, salutation to the one who granted permission for the decapitation while absorbed in meditative concentration (*samādhi*). Oṃ, salutation to the one who dwells in solitude. Oṃ, salutation to the Yogin. (830) Oṃ, salutation to the one whose mind is dissolved in meditative concentration.

Oṃ, salutation to him from whom all mental constructs have departed through the contemplation of the Supreme Self. Oṃ, salutation to him whose body is motionless. Oṃ, salutation to him who is free from delusion. Oṃ, salutation to him whose nature is uninterrupted bliss. Oṃ, salutation to him who perceived the arrival of the Kāpālika intent on his own murder. Oṃ, salutation to him whose chin is placed against the region of the Adam’s apple. Oṃ, salutation to him whose gaze is fixed upon the tip of the nose. Oṃ, salutation to him seated in the Siddhāsana posture. Oṃ, salutation to him from whom the notion of duality has vanished. ||840||

Oṃ, salutations to him whose mind is immersed in the waves of supreme bliss consisting of pure consciousness. Oṃ, salutations to him who did not heed the Kāpālika’s efforts to kill him with a sword. Oṃ, salutations to him who destroyed his own enemies once he had learned the facts regarding the lotus-feet [of Viṣṇu]. Oṃ, salutations to him who was shaken by the martial prowess displayed at the lotus-feet of Nṛsiṃha while in the guise of that deity. Oṃ, salutations to him whose intellect has emerged from meditative absorption (samādhi). Oṃ, salutations to him whose eyes have been opened. Oṃ, salutations to him whose ears were deafened by the sound of that loud, boisterous laughter.

Oṃ, salutations to the illustrious Nṛhari, who reveals himself to those with mouths made formidable by fangs. Oṃ, salutations to him whose inner being was rendered motionless by the sudden glance of Nṛsiṃha. Oṃ, salutations to the fearless one. Oṃ, salutations to him whose tears flowed from overflowing bliss. Oṃ, salutations to him who is intent on offering praise. Oṃ, salutations to him who is devoted to praying for the pacification of Nṛsiṃha’s wrath. Oṃ, salutations to the ascetic. Oṃ, salutations to him who showed Padmapāda, who was agitated by the possession of Nṛsiṃha.

Oṃ, salutations to him who bowed at the lotus feet of the Knower of his own dream-like experiences; oṃ, salutations to him who was filled with wonder; oṃ, salutations to him who wandered in the vicinity of Gokarṇa; oṃ, salutations to him who prostrated at the lotus feet of Gokarṇeśvara; oṃ, salutations to him whose mind was full of joy; oṃ, salutations to him who offered praise to the Lord of Gokarṇa; oṃ, salutations to him who was intent on remaining there for three nights; oṃ, salutations to him whose intellect was fulfilled by the vision of the Great Goddess Mūkāmbikā; oṃ, salutations to him who beheld a brahmin couple.

Oṃ, salutations to him whose mind was distressed by that weeping. Oṃ, salutations to him who was pained at the sight of the dead infant lying on his lap. Oṃ, salutations to him whose ears were filled with the words of Anaṅga. Oṃ, salutations to him who longed for the restoration of his son to life. Oṃ, salutations to him whose own greatness was described by the twice-born. Oṃ, salutations to the protector of all. Oṃ, salutations to him whose mind was gladdened by the revival of his son occurring at that very moment. Oṃ, salutations to him who caused wonder in those who witnessed his own majesty.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who desires the vision of Mūkāmbā. Oṃ, salutations to the one intent upon dwelling in that sacred field (kṣetra). Oṃ, salutations to the one who takes delight in composing hymns of profound meaning in various high and low meters. Oṃ, salutations to the one who serves the village of Śrībali, which abounds in Brahmins devoted to their own duties. Oṃ, salutations to the one who dispelled the childhood innocence of the virtuous Brahmin boy named Prabhākara. Oṃ, salutations to the one eager to bestow grace upon those Brahmins who have come for refuge at his feet. Oṃ, salutations to the one intent on raising up both the one who prostrates and his son.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who heard the words and the innocent gestures of that son described by the twice-born. Oṃ, salutations to the one who beheld the twice-born boy, who resembled a fire concealed within. Oṃ, salutations to the one who knew the particular greatness of that [boy]. Oṃ, salutations to the one who broke the seal of silence. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose mind was intent on making inquiries of the twice-born boy. Oṃ, salutations to the one who questioned the cause of his dullness. Oṃ, salutations to the mine of compassion. Oṃ, salutations to the one who was eager to hear those words while disguised in the dress of a child.

Oṃ, homage to him who is utterly amazed by the words of the child, which awaken the realization that the body and so forth are insentient. Oṃ, homage to him who is intent on praising those words, having awakened his own consciousness. Oṃ, homage to him who is eager to praise the wisdom of the author of the *Padyadvādaśikā*. Oṃ, homage to him who rejoices in those utterances that manifest the knowledge of reality. Oṃ, homage to him who is utterly amazed by the wisdom of the child, despite being devoid of formal instruction and the like. Oṃ, homage to him who is intent upon bestowing grace upon him. Oṃ, homage to him who placed his hand upon the child’s head.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrates the unsuitability of dwelling in a household. Oṃ, salutations to the one intent on praise. Oṃ, salutations to the one engaged in sending forth the twice-born. Oṃ, salutations to the one engaged in gathering disciples. Oṃ, salutations to the one who bestowed the name Hastāmalaka. Oṃ, salutations to the one who conferred the *nyāsa* initiation. Oṃ, salutations to the one who took refuge in Hastāmalaka, who had attained the state of being his own disciple. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose mind was intent on going to the excellent sacred field known as Śṛṅgagiri. Oṃ, salutations to the one who performed his ablutions in the Tuṅgabhadrā river.

Oṃ, salutation to him who is eager to expound the commentaries. Oṃ, salutation to the builder of the temple of Śāradā. Oṃ, salutation to him who is intent upon the installation of Śāradā. Oṃ, salutation to him who is devoted to the worship of Śāradā. Oṃ, salutation to him whose face is like the autumnal moon. Oṃ, salutation to him whose mind is pleased by the service of his own excellent disciple named Giri. Oṃ, salutation to him who is adorned by a circle of disciples seated for the purpose of study. Oṃ, salutation to him who, while intent on washing his own garment, observed Giri’s arrival.
