Oṃ, salutations to the one intent on dispelling the malice of his own disciples. Oṃ, salutations to the one solely devoted to bestowing grace upon his excellent disciple named Giri. Oṃ, salutations to the one praised by Giri, who attained the state of omniscience through his grace. Oṃ, salutations to the one saluted by Giri, who has mastered all true sciences. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose ears were filled with the beautiful verses of the excellent poem titled *Toṭaka*. Oṃ, salutations to the one whose majesty, even as a mere fragment of compassion, was fully recognized by other disciples.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who manifested the greatness of the Guru’s grace. ||920|| Oṃ, salutations to the one who sustains the world. Oṃ, salutations to the one who bestowed the name Toṭaka. Oṃ, salutations to the one highly honored by the venerable Toṭakācārya. Oṃ, salutations to the one who contemplates the majesty of the style of his speech, which contains the essence of reality. Oṃ, salutations to the one who rests upon the hand-like lotus-feet of the noble Sureśvarācārya. Oṃ, salutations to the one followed by Toṭaka. Oṃ, salutations to the one supported by the four disciples.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who composed the *Bhāṣya* and *Vārtika* as requested by Sureśvara. Oṃ, salutations to the giver of permission for the composition of the *Vārtika*. Oṃ, salutations to the preeminent among teachers (*deśikapuṅgava*). Oṃ, salutations to the one awakened by the lotus-feet of [Śaṅkara] and others, who dispelled the doubts regarding the departure from the established doctrine (*siddhānta*). Oṃ, salutations to the one who perceived the obstacles that arose during the creation of the *Vārtika* treatise. Oṃ, salutations to the one who followed the persistent entreaties of his disciples. Oṃ, salutations to the one who is a mine of compassion for the multitude of disciples.

Oṃ, salutations to him who examined the commentary and sub-commentary composed by Padmapāda; Oṃ, salutations to him who studied the works of Sureśvara, such as the *Ramyanaishkarmyasiddhi*; Oṃ, salutations to him whose mind was delighted by seeing the composition of the beginning and end of the treatises; Oṃ, salutations to him who was greatly amazed upon seeing his skill in composing the treatise; Oṃ, salutations to him who was eager to compose his own commentary and gloss on the *Taittirīya Upaniṣad*; Oṃ, salutations to him who was devoted to hearing the excellent *Vārttika* on the true commentary of the *Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad*. ||940||

Oṃ, salutations to the one who examined the series of non-dualistic treatises composed by many disciples. Oṃ, salutations to the one who reflected upon the words of Padmapāda, who was inspired to undertake a pilgrimage to sacred sites (tīrthayātrā). Oṃ, salutations to the one who demonstrated the multitude of various faults arising from such pilgrimages. Oṃ, salutations to the one who established the occurrence of thousands of diverse distractions. Oṃ, salutations to the one who approved of Padmapāda’s singular persistence in the pilgrimage. Oṃ, salutations to the one who lamented for Padmapāda, who would not listen to his own words of instruction. Oṃ, salutations to the one who clearly showed the defects of the path and other such matters.

Oṃ, salutations to the one who awakens through wakefulness. Oṃ, salutations to the one distressed by the memory of his own mother as death approached. Oṃ, salutations to the one who went to his mother’s side upon merely being remembered. Oṃ, salutations to the one possessed of supreme devotion. Oṃ, salutations to the one delighted by the sight of his mother. Oṃ, salutations to the one who gladdened his own mother. Oṃ, salutations to the one who fulfilled the desire of his mother, who prayed solely for his spiritual refinement (*saṃskāra*). Oṃ, salutations to the teacher of the Supreme Brahman known as Tāraka. Oṃ, salutations to the Supreme Lord.

Oṃ, salutations to the one solely intent on rescuing his mother, who was ignorant of Brahman. Oṃ, salutations to the one who revealed the Supreme Lord who had arrived through his own hymn of praise. Oṃ, salutations to the one who beheld the fear of his mother. Oṃ, salutations to the one intent upon the hymns of Mādhava. (960) Oṃ, salutations to the one who revealed the form of Viṣṇu attained through the greatness of that hymn. Oṃ, salutations to the one who became the vessel for the mother’s joy arising from that vision. Oṃ, salutations to the one who brought about the vision of his mother seated in the celestial chariot of Viṣṇu’s messenger.

Oṃ, salutation to him who made an effort to perform the purificatory rites (*saṃskāra*). Oṃ, salutation to him who summoned his circle of kinsmen. Oṃ, salutation to him who prayed to the fire for the sake of the purificatory rites. Oṃ, salutation to him who was rejected by his circle of kinsmen. Oṃ, salutation to the Mother (Mātṛkā) who was consecrated by the fire obtained through the churning of Dakṣa’s arm. Oṃ, salutation to him who inflicted the curse of being excluded from the Vedas upon his own people who failed to offer the fire. Oṃ, salutation to him who spoke of the absence of alms for ascetics (*yatibhikṣā*). Oṃ, salutation to him who turned that house into a cremation ground (*śmaśāna*). Oṃ, salutation to him who desired the arrival of Padmapāda.

Oṃ, salutation to him who made his dwelling in that place. Oṃ, salutation to him who was intent upon beholding the Lord of Mahāsurālaya. Oṃ, salutation to him who is proficient in the arrival of the group of disciples. Oṃ, salutation to him who prompts inquiries regarding their welfare. Oṃ, salutation to him who listens to the account of all his own circumstances as they were awakened by the lotus-feet [of Śaṅkara]. Oṃ, salutation to him who grieves for the millions of commentaries previously consumed by fire. Oṃ, salutation to him who leads Padmapāda, who was despondent due to the loss of those commentaries.

Oṃ, homage to the one who heard the extremely fierce speech of those administering poison that causes the dullness of wisdom. Oṃ, homage to the one who felt compassion for Padmapāda as he fell at his own feet. Oṃ, homage to the one who contemplated the five verses found in the previously mentioned commentary. Oṃ, homage to the one who elucidated every subject contained within those five verses. Oṃ, homage to the one who honored Padmapāda and others, being satisfied by the writing of the commentary. Oṃ, homage to the one whose majesty was praised by the multitude of his own astonished disciples.

Oṃ, salutation to the one who brought about the meditative absorption of the Lord of Kerala, who was afflicted by the suffering of the misfortune of the drama. Oṃ, salutation to the one who astonished the lords of men with the narration of the aforementioned drama. Oṃ, salutation to the one accompanied by the noble disciple King Sudhanvan. Oṃ, salutation to the one resplendent in victory. Oṃ, salutation to the one who performed ablutions at the Rāmasetu. ||990|| Oṃ, salutation to the one whose enthusiasm for victory lies in the Śākta lineage. Oṃ, salutation to the one who found bliss in wandering through the regions of Kāñcī, Vidarbha, Karṇāṭa, and Tada. Oṃ, salutation to the conqueror of the hosts of Kāpālikas.

Oṃ, salutations to the one radiant with victory over Nīlakaṇṭha. Oṃ, salutations to the one who bestows happiness upon those who possess secret knowledge of the rites of exorcism (*abhicāra*). Oṃ, salutations to the one whose intellect is immersed in the ocean of bliss from the vision of the noble Gauḍapāda. Oṃ, salutations to the one who reveals the seat of Śāradā shining in the land of Kaśmīra. Oṃ, salutations to the one radiant with victory over the hosts of disputants seated at the southern gate. Oṃ, salutations to the one eager for the ascent to the throne of omniscience once victory has been attained.

Oṃ, homage to the one whose form is completely covered by a rain of excellent flowers offered by the deities. Oṃ, homage to the one who is filled with supreme bliss upon going to Mount Kailāsa. Oṃ, homage to the one invoked by Brahmā and the other gods. Oṃ, homage to the one to whom the assembly of disciples has prostrated. Oṃ, homage to the one intent on mounting the great bull. Oṃ, homage to the one whose hand is placed by the Lotus-born (Brahmā). Oṃ, homage to the one devoted to fulfilling all desires. Oṃ, homage to the one whose inner being is liberated.
Oṃ, salutations to the one who is filled with supreme bliss upon departing for the mountain of Śrī Kailāsa. Oṃ, salutations to the venerable True Guru, the Supreme Brahman. Oṃ. ||1008||

May the sovereign ascetic Śaṅkaradeśikendra, the sole sun for dispelling the inner darkness, the unique rain-cloud for extinguishing the fierce flames of the fire of the three-fold afflictions, the submarine fire for the ocean of suffering, and the rising moon for the nectar-ocean of wisdom-bliss, shine eternally within the sky of my heart.

Bow down to the feet of the most excellent Śaṅkara-guru, who cuts through the darkness in the hearts of his devotees like the sun; who is the supreme Garuḍa to the venomous serpents of the dualities of pleasure and pain; and who is the son of the pitcher-born Agastya for the great ocean of birth, death, and misfortune.
Victory, victory to Śaṅkara! Om, salutations to the Supreme Brahman, the venerable Candramaulīśvara, together with the supreme sovereign lady, the illustrious Lalitā Mahātripurasundarī.
